tldr: A workspace owner can now invite a colleague by e-mail from the workspace settings or the API. The colleague opens a one-time link, sets a password and joins as a member; the owner sees open invitations and can cancel them. Two Critical findings block the merge: a link works more than once, and an expired link still lets the colleague in.
title: Workspace invitations
description: The change lets a workspace owner invite a colleague by e-mail. The colleague accepts through a one-time link and joins as a member. Invitations are stored with a token and an expiry, the owner can list and cancel open invitations, and both the web settings and the API can send them.

areas.summary: The owner sends an invitation from the settings or the API; the e-mail carries the link. Open invitations are listed and can be cancelled.
A new invitation record holds the e-mail, the token, the expiry and the acceptance time.
The link signs the colleague up and adds them to the workspace as a member.

diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Owner
  participant InvitationController
  participant Mail
  participant Colleague
  participant InvitationAcceptController
  Owner->>InvitationController: Send invitation (e-mail)
  InvitationController->>Mail: Queue invitation e-mail with token link
  Mail-->>Colleague: Invitation e-mail
  Colleague->>InvitationAcceptController: Open link with token
  InvitationAcceptController-->>Colleague: Set password, join workspace

test_routes.try: Send an invitation to a new e-mail, see it in the open list, cancel it.
Send the 21st invitation of the day and check it is refused.
Open the link, set a password, join; open the same link again and an 8-day-old link — both must show "This invitation is no longer valid".
